title: The Man Who Lived in an Iron Lung for 70 Years

sections.name: The Man Who Lived in an Iron Lung for 70 Years

lines.top: THE MAN WHO LIVED IN AN

lines: In the 1950s, hospitals were filled with rows of giant metal tubes.
They were iron lungs. Polio could paralyse the muscles you breathe with, so the machine breathed for you.
It changed the air pressure around your body, pulling your chest open, then letting it fall.
In 1952, a six year old boy called Paul Alexander was put inside one.
He spent most of his life in it, but still became a lawyer, and wrote a book, typing with a stick held in his mouth.
He lived in his iron lung for more than seventy years. Thanks to the polio vaccine, almost no one needs one now.
